name: Badacey
description: Badacey is a high-skill, split-pot poker variant that combines the unique hand-building of Badugi with the classic Ace-to-Five Lowball. Players are dealt five cards and undergo three rounds of drawing to create two distinct winning combinations: a 4-card Badugi hand (all different suits and ranks) and a 5-card Lowball hand. It is a 'mixed game' favorite in high-stakes circles, prized for its complex mathematical crossovers.

overview.description: Badacey is a high-skill, split-pot poker variant that combines the unique hand-building of Badugi with the classic Ace-to-Five Lowball. Players are dealt five cards and undergo three rounds of drawing to create two distinct winning combinations: a 4-card Badugi hand (all different suits and ranks) and a 5-card Lowball hand. It is a 'mixed game' favorite in high-stakes circles, prized for its complex mathematical crossovers.

history.origins: Developed in the early 2000s in Las Vegas and California card rooms as part of the 'Mixed Game' movement. It was created to merge the popularity of Badugi with the more established Ace-to-Five Lowball format.
timeline: 2004: Badugi gains popularity in North American poker rooms.
2008: Badacey emerges as a staple in 'H.O.R.S.E.'-style mixed games.
Present: Frequently played in the World Series of Poker (WSOP) dealer's choice events.
history.cultural: Known as a 'Thinker's Game', often played with blinds and a fixed-limit betting structure.
history.evolution: The game was designed to reduce the 'luck' factor of single-pot Lowball by forcing players to manage two different ranking systems simultaneously.

setup.players: Two to six players. All players post an ante; the dealer gives each player five cards face down. Play uses a dealer button with small and big blinds; the game is commonly played with fixed-limit betting in card rooms.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face down. There are three drawing rounds where players can discard 0-5 cards and receive replacements.
setup.equipment: Poker chips, Dealer button, Small/Big Blind markers.

rules.objective: Win half the pot with the best 4-card Badugi and half with the best 5-card Ace-to-Five low.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Blinds**: Players post small and big blinds. 2. **Deal**: 5 cards each. 3. **Betting Round 1**. 4. **First Draw**: Players discard and draw. 5. **Betting Round 2**. 6. **Second Draw**. 7. **Betting Round 3**. 8. **Third Draw**. 9. **Final Betting Round**. 10. **Showdown**: Split pot.
keyRules: A 3-card Badugi loses to any 4-card Badugi.
In the Lowball half, if you have a pair, your low is disqualified from the top ranks.
A-2-3-4-5 is the best low; A-2-3-4 (rainbow) is the best Badugi.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Lowball half first. A solid A-2-3-4-5 low will almost always guarantee you a 4-card Badugi attempt. It is much easier to scoop with a strong low.
strategy.intermediate: Draw heavy early. If you don't have three cards to a good low or Badugi, discard all five cards in the first round. Don't fall in love with a King-high Badugi.
strategy.advanced: Snowing: A bluffing technique where you stand pat (draw zero cards) as if you have a perfect hand, forcing opponents to fold their drawing hands even if you actually have nothing.
tips: Aces represent double value in Badacey: they are the best card for both the Low and the Badugi halves.
Pay attention to 'folded' cards if the game allows peeking at the muck; it tells you which low cards are out of play.

variations.name: Badeucy
variations.description: Uses Deuce-to-Seven rules for the low half instead of Ace-to-Five.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is described at a rules level; specific engine overrides for Badeucy are not yet modeled.

scoring.winCondition: Lowest ranks in two specific categories.

synthesis.shortDescription: Test your stamina in the world of high-stakes mixed poker. Badacey combines the 4-card suit-tracking of Badugi with the 5-card minimalism of Ace-to-Five lowball. With three draws and two pots on the line, only the most disciplined players survive the showdown.
